      <description>Britisk politi bekrefter overfor BBC at de har innledet en etterforskning mot komikeren David Walliams for alvorlige seksuelle forbrytelser.

      <description>Microsoft opplever tekniske problemer som rammer brukere av blant annet e-posttjenesten Outlook og Teams. Selskapet opplyser at de jobber med å løse saken.
Også andre Microsoft-produkter er berørt, blant annet SharePoint og Planner.
Årsaken er at en del av infrastrukturen opplevde «forhøyet belastning, ifølge Microsoft. Selskapet fant ut at en rekke servere var «uventet utilgjengelige».
Ifølge nettstedet Downdetector nådde problemene et høydepunkt ved 19-tiden norsk tid, med 129 476 feilmeldinger.
Ved 5.30-tiden natt til fredag har antallet feilmeldinger falt til 21 988.</description>

      <description>En buss kjørte i dag tidlig av veien i Røn i Vestre Slidre.
Politiet opplyser at bussen skal ha sklidd av veien i lav hastighet, men at den ligger på siden.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/skolebuss-av-veien-i-larvik-1.18079991</link>
      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Norge gir 600 regnskogmillioner til Brasil</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norge-gir-600-regnskogmillioner-til-brasil-1.18077109</link>
      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.
– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.
Brasil har det siste året redusert avskogningen til det laveste nivået siden målingene staret for over 40 år siden.
Gjennom den norske regnskogsatsingen gir Norge økonomisk støtte til Brasil når de klarer å redusere avskogingen.
– Norge finansierer resultater, og nå har vi med oss finansiering av de gode resultatene i Brasil, sier Aasland.</description>

Influence Board Shop hopes to trade profits for purpose, keeping its doors open as a hub for skateboarding, youth development and community connection.

On a grey, rainy day in Victoria, an empty skate park is nothing unusual. But at Influence Board Shop on Quadra Street, the quiet reflects something bigger: a business preparing for a major change.

After 15 years as a fixture in Victoria’s skateboarding community, Influence is looking to transition into a non-profit organization.

Owner Steve Munro says the skateboarding retail business has taken a hit in recent years.

“The skateboarding business, as I know and everyone else in my industry knows, has really gone down dramatically in the last few years,” he says.

Rather than give up the space, Munro is looking to change the business model and its purpose.

“We’re trying to pivot into a non-profit kind of formula, and just kind of open up this space, not to make money because that’s never really been our goal.”

The property includes a retail shop, three indoor skate parks, a stage for all-ages shows and a planned café. Munro wants to make those facilities more accessible, with a focus on health and recreation, youth development and community improvement.

A non-profit structure could also open the door to funding opportunities, including youth sports grants.

But first, the resident director of boards needs a board of directors, among other things. He’s looking for volunteers with professional experience who are willing to lend their skills to the cause.

“We’re looking for volunteers as far as someone who knows law, someone who knows accounting,” he says.

The bigger ambition is to give back to a community that has changed his life and make skateboarding more welcoming to everyone, including newcomers who may not know a kickflip from a kickstand.

For regulars like Dylon, the space is already making a difference. He’s recently returned to skateboarding and now visits twice a week.

“Started getting back into it, coming here two times a week now,” he says.

Asked if he’s hooked, his answer is emphatic: “I’m hooked!”

Munro says the skateboarding community has always been supportive, despite the sport’s sometimes rebellious reputation. And with skateboarding now an Olympic sport, he thinks perceptions are changing.

“Now that we’re in the Olympics, we’re not really the bad guys in TV shows anymore. We’re kinda the good guys,” he says with a smile.

In May, Chan, 39, was sentenced to 4.5 years in prison for convictions of voyeurism, making child pornography, publishing recordings obtained through a crime, and breaching court ordered conditions.

Saanich Police began investigating Chan after a January 2024 tip flagged that an account in Saanich was uploading voyeuristic images. That account brought police to Chan.

The ongoing saga of the shipbreaking facility in Union Bay will be heard in the Supreme Court of British Columbia at the end of November.

The Comox Valley Regional District (CVRD) said it has learned the court dates will be Nov. 25, 26 and 27.

The notice of civil claim was initially filed on April 14, 2022, then an amended notice expanding the claim was filed on March 25, 2026.

The CVRD’s amended claim against Union Bay Industries and Deep Water Recovery is that the companies are using the property for a number of purposes that are not allowed.

The property is zoned in two pieces, with the shoreline zoned for Industrial Marine. The land is partially zoned for Rural Twenty and another portion for Country Residential One.

The Industrial Marine zoning allows for uses such as boat building and repairs and service and sales, seafood processing and sales, marina, barge facility, waterfront freight handling facility, log handling and storage facility, storage and works yard and warehousing, and offices.

The Rural Twenty, or land-based portion, allows for a single-detached dwelling, agricultural use, veterinary establishment, plant nursery and greenhouse, silviculture, fish hatchery, animal kennel, riding academy, wood processing, sawmill, various gravel and peat uses, or a research and testing facility.

The Country residential portion only allows for a single detached dwelling or agriculture use.

The CVRD’s claim alleges that the property was being used for industrial purposes and dismantling and recycling marine vessels.

“The Ship Breaking Use is not a permitted use of the Property under the Zoning Bylaw, and is prohibited by the Zoning Bylaw,” the CVRD’s claim says.

Additionally, the claim alleges the land is being used to house people in recreational vehicles, which is not a permitted use.

The CVRD is seeking a declaration that the ship breaking and housing use are in contravention of its zoning bylaw, an order that the companies must cease and desist the ship breaking, and that the housing use must cease and desist as well, in addition to other relief.

In the response by Union Bay Industries and Deep Water Recovery, the only facts agreed to from the CVRD’s claim are that the two companies are incorporated and their respective addresses, that Union Bay Industries is the registered owner in fee simple, and that Deep Water occupies the property.

“Unless expressly admitted herein, the Defendents deny each and every allegation of fact, argument, and all other matters contained in the Plaintiff’s Amended Notice of Civil Claim,” the response says.

The response says that Union Bay Industries previously operated a log sorting business on the property, and that Deep Water Recovery’s operations include a barge loading facility, a storage and works yard and warehousing facility, a waterfront freight handling facility, and marine vessel services.

“Deep Water has, on occasion, been tasked with performing emergency rescue services on behalf of the Canadian government and the Canadian Coast Guard,” the response says.

“To date, Deep Water’s activities have never included work on any motorized vessels, with the exception of one small wooden vessel delivered by the Canadian Coast Guard, as referenced above.”

The response also claims that the CVRD “previously approved Deep Water’s operations, and, on its own admission, considered those operations to be compliant with the Zoning Bylaw,” the response says.

“However, after sustained lobbying by local residents and organized community groups, the Plaintiff succumbed to external pressure and saw Deep Water’s operations as politically unpopular.”

The response claims the enforcement has been advanced “without any legitimate regulatory objective.”

“Instead, the Plaintiff has invoked enforcement and other mechanisms, including the Court’s processes, not to enforce its bylaws, but to eliminate a disfavoured, yet lawful, business after previously approving it.”

The response argues that its operations are permitted under the boat building and repairs and service and sales, barge facility, waterfront freight handling facility and/or storage works yard and warehousing uses in the zoning.

The property was previously governed by a water lease agreement with the province of B.C., which was cancelled on or around July 3, 2025.

It alleges its application to the B.C. government included information that it provides a vessel decommissioning service, the services consist of decommissioning derelict vessels or those at the end of its serviceable life, and that it would conform with the international quality management standards for effective environmental management.

The response further alleges that the CVRD wrote a letter to the ministry in response to the proposed tenure, confirming that the purposes fit the zoning.

The companies also deny housing individuals on the site in recreational vehicles or at all.

The response says that it opposes granting all requested relief sought by the CVRD.

The trial will be heard in court in Vancouver from Nov. 25-27.

Airports across the country have suspended flights to and from the United States after the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration issued a countrywide ground stop order, though Nav Canada says there is no direct impact on its systems.

The order, which grounded all flights in the United States on Friday afternoon, cited communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.

Several Canadian airports, including in Montreal and Toronto, have reported that all flights to and from the United States are suspended.

The Toronto Pearson International Airport said international and domestic flights continue to operate where routes do not require transit through U.S. airspace. It also said it’s increasing staffing across the airport to assist affected passengers. 

“Our support teams are being deployed throughout the terminals, with additional resources available in the U.S. departures area,” said a social media post from the airport. “We are also working closely with airlines and have implemented a parking plan for aircraft.”

Red bars across Air Canada’s U.S. check-in counters signalled trouble for travellers at Toronto Pearson.

Passengers stood with their luggage, repeatedly refreshing their phones and looking for answers from airport staff. 

For Kelly Adenike, who was trying to get to Punta Cana in the Dominican Republic, the question is whether she’ll make it out of Pearson at all or end up back home in Kitchener, Ont.

“This really sucks,” she said. “Do they expect me to go home? Could they call it off soon? Maybe let us know if we can wait until midnight?”

Nav Canada, a privately run, non-profit corporation that operates Canada’s civil air navigation system, said there is no direct impact on its operations and it continues to support the safe movement of air traffic in Canada’s airspace, including any aircraft that may be diverted.

It said its systems were operating normally and recommended that anyone flying to or from the United States check with their airline.

Samantha Chowen said the airplane doors had just closed on her flight from Nashville to Toronto when the captain announced that the plane would not be able to take off due to an unforeseen issue with air traffic control. After about an hour, she said, passengers were asked to deplane.

Chowen, who lives in Regina, said she has been told not to expect to fly home to Canada on Friday but to get a hotel and wait for further notice. 

“They said they will be emailing us shortly with a rerouted flight but that right now they can’t guarantee when that will be,” said Chowen. “Kind of just sit and wait I guess.”

Chowen, who has been on a weeklong trip, said she tore her ACL on the third day of her vacation. 

“I’ve been hobbling around just trying to get home,” said Chowen. “As long as I’m home by Monday to make my MRI, this is fine.”

Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said in a media statement the Nav Canada measures will help “safely manage traffic volumes.”

“I want to reassure Canadians that our air traffic management systems continue to function normally,” he said.

MacKinnon also said Canada has offered its full assistance to the Federal Aviation Administration as it manages the situation, including accommodation of U.S.-bound aircraft as required.  

“We remain ready to provide support to our American colleagues as the situation evolves,” said MacKinnon. 

Krista Kealey, spokesperson for the Ottawa International Airport Authority, said U.S. arrivals and departures are being affected at the airport.

She said the airport is expecting diversions, although it understands that international flights bound for the United States will be handled on a case-by-case basis.

Yasmine Mehdi, an Air Canada spokesperson, said the ground stop is affecting flights to and from the United States. She said flights to and from the Caribbean and South America may also be affected.

“Any flights currently airborne have been advised they are permitted to continue,” said Mehdi. “We are monitoring the situation very closely and will provide updates as they become available.”

WestJet said in a media statement that it’s closely monitoring the situation and will keep guests informed of any impacts to their travel plans. The airline said it’s following “all regulatory direction.”

The Vancouver International Airport said airlines are adjusting flight schedules, which is causing cancellations to U.S. destinations, and some delays and cancellations to international and domestic flights.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communications issue was affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centres that direct planes travelling between airports countrywide. He said FAA technicians are investigating.

This is the first countrywide ground stop in the United States since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. The last such shutdown prior to 2023 happened after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the ground stop was due to a “telecommunication outage.”

“This isn’t a safety to the American people, or another 9/11,” he said. “I think that’s what a lot of people are trying to make the comparison to, and that’s not the case.”

The Village of Port Alice is issuing a warning after a wild Canada goose has tested positive for avian flu.

“A rescued goose, close to town, tested positive, so we are ensuring the community is aware and can take extra precautions,” the Village of Port Alice said in a Facebook post.

“Bird flu mainly affects birds, and the risk to most people is low.”

The village’s Facebook post says a bird that was rescued, was brought to MARS Wildlife Rescue then tested and that the bird was found on the highway close to town.

Port Alice is advising residents to not feed wild birds.

“We need to lessen contact with wild birds,” the post says. “There is plenty of natural food for them, and they will not suffer.”

Additionally, the village says to keep your dogs on a leash near where wild birds gather, and do not let them sniff, pick up, or eat sick or dead birds, or come in contact with bird droppings.

If you think your dog was exposed, call your veterinarian.

Parents should also teach their children to leave sick or dead birds alone, as well as loose feathers.

“If your child touches a sick or dead bird, wash their hands with soap and water and contact your health care provider or local public health office promptly for advice,” the village says.

If you keep backyard chickens, you’re advised to keep them in a covered run or enclosure that keeps wild birds out and keep feed and drinking water where wild birds can’t reach.

Make sure to use a separate pair of boots in the coop, and wash your hands with soap and water after caring for your flock.

Anyone who notices sudden deaths, breathing problems, or a sharp drop in egg laying for their flock is advised to call your veterinarian or the Canadian Food Inspection Agency.

“Keep sick birds on your property while you wait for instructions,” the village says.
